◆ BLOCK PARTY ACADEMY
01 / THE CONTROLS

YOU'RE IN CONTROL

▲◀◆▶▼
SWAP

Phone / tablet: use the D-pad to move your cursor and tap SWAP to exchange blocks. Tap RAISE ROW to bring in a new row.

Keyboard: arrow keys move the cursor, Space swaps. You can change which side holds the D-pad in Difficulty & Game Options.

02 / HOW TO MOVE

SWAP TO SCORE

◆●★■ ▲●▲◆ ■●★▲

The cursor brackets select two blocks side by side. All swaps are horizontal only—you cannot swap blocks vertically. Press SWAP to exchange the selected blocks. Plan ahead: falling blocks can create new matches and chains!

Make larger matches for combos, and keep clearing blocks to build your score.

03 / THE BASICS

MAKE A MATCH!

◆▲●★■▲ ●◆▲■★● ★▲▲▲◆■

Line up three or more matching blocks horizontally or vertically to clear them. Blocks above fall into the empty spaces.

04 / EVERYDAY BLOCKS

FIVE COLORS. ONE GOAL.

◆Red DiamondMatch with red
●Blue CircleMatch with blue
▲Green TriangleMatch with green
★Yellow StarMatch with yellow
■Purple SquareMatch with purple

Normal blocks match by color and symbol. Look for three or more in a row or column.

05 / COMBOS

MORE BLOCKS, MORE POINTS!

●●●●●
5-BLOCK COMBO! +700

Match four or more blocks in a single group for a combo bonus. Each normal block is worth 100 points, plus 100 extra points for every block beyond the first three.

3 blocks = 300 pointsBasic match, no combo bonus.
4 blocks = 500 points400 base + 100 combo bonus.
5 blocks = 700 points500 base + 200 combo bonus.

These are base scores, before any speed or chain multiplier.

06 / SPEED MULTIPLIERS

BEAT THE CLEAR!

◆◆◆
SWAP AGAIN WHILE THESE CLEAR!
SPEED ×1.5 → ×2 → ×2.5

After making a match, move quickly and swap another pair to create a new match while the first blocks are still visibly clearing.

Your second overlapping manual match earns ×1.5, the next overlapping match earns ×2, then ×2.5, and so on. Each successful overlapping match raises the multiplier by 0.5.

Important: waiting until the first clear finishes won't count. Automatic matches caused by falling blocks aren't speed matches.

07 / GRAVITY CHAINS

LET THEM FALL!

■ ■ ◆ ◆ ◆ ■
① MATCH 3 RED!② RED CLEARS · PURPLE FALLS ↓③ PURPLE MATCH · CHAIN ×2!
↻ REPEATING DEMO

Make a match that causes blocks above it to fall into another match. That's a gravity chain: the second linked clear scores ×2, the third ×4, and the fourth ×8.

Plan the blocks above your match so they line up after falling. Only matches linked to the previous clear by gravity qualify—not just any match made soon afterward.

Combos increase the base points first. A gravity-chain multiplier then multiplies those points.

08 / POWER BLOCKS

SPECIAL DELIVERY!

💣BombClears blocks next to a matched Bomb group.
⇄SwapAfter five swaps, explodes and clears nearby blocks.
⚡ShockClears blocks of one color across the board.

Watch your score! In Solo, blocks destroyed by special effects cost −100 points each. Matched blocks still earn points normally.

09 / VERSUS POWER BLOCKS

TURN THE TABLES

−NegativeFor 10 seconds, the opponent’s earned match points generate blocks sent to your board.
☠SkullDrops a solid, full-width garbage row on the opponent.
PoisonInfects three opponent blocks for 15 seconds; swapping infected blocks can spread it.Poison creates garbage: Each poisoned block you match creates a three-block-wide garbage slab on your own board. If you match none before the poison wears off, you receive one six-block-wide poison slab instead. Match beside garbage to break it apart.
💣⚡⇄Original Special BlocksBomb, Swap, and Shock also attack your opponent in Versus.For every block their effects destroy, the opponent receives one block (1:1)—whether the destroyed block is normal or special.
10 / GARBAGE BLOCKS

BREAK THE GARBAGE!

☠
▲▲▲
MATCH ADJACENT BLOCKS TO BREAK THE SLAB
☣
PINK GARBAGE COMES FROM POISON

Garbage blocks are solid obstacles sent by attacks. You can't swap them or match them directly.

Make a match of three or more ordinary blocks directly beside or below/above garbage. The entire connected garbage slab breaks into regular colored blocks that you can then match.

Poison connection: matching an infected block creates a three-block-wide garbage slab on your own board for each poisoned block in the match. Get rid of poison before it spreads!

11 / CHAIN GARBAGE

RAINBOW CHAIN ATTACK!

In Versus, gravity chains send a special rainbow garbage slab to your opponent after the entire chain finishes. A bigger chain sends a taller slab!

CHAIN ×2
1 row high
CHAIN ×3
2 rows high
CHAIN ×4
3 rows high
CHAIN ×5
4 rows high

One solid block: Each attack fills the board's entire six-column width. Taller blocks are one continuous multicolored slab, not separate rows stacked together.

HOW TO BREAK IT
3 rows

✓Cleared

Match ordinary blocks touching the slab to turn its bottom row into normal blocks. The remaining rainbow slab becomes one row shorter. Repeat until the whole slab is gone.

12 / GAME MODES

PICK YOUR CHALLENGE

Line ClearClear or lower every block below the target line.
Timed PlayEarn as many points as possible before the timer ends.
Unlimited Play (Solo)Keep playing for as long as you can survive.
Special Battle (Versus)Use special attacks to outlast the computer.

In Practice Line Clear, rows only rise when you choose to raise them. Other difficulties bring more pressure!

13 / GAMEPLAY DIFFICULTY

SET THE PACE

Practice · Line Clear onlyNo automatic rising rows. Raise a row only when you want to.
EasyRows rise slowly, giving you more time to plan matches.
MediumRows rise faster, with more pressure as the board grows.
HardRows rise fastest and accelerate as you progress.

Gameplay difficulty changes the speed of rising rows. In Line Clear, it also changes how deep the target line starts: Easy is shallower, Hard is deeper.

14 / COMPUTER DIFFICULTY

CHOOSE YOUR RIVAL

Easy CPUMoves about every 1.5 seconds. Mostly tries random swaps, occasionally spotting matches.
Medium CPUMoves about every 0.75 seconds. Usually chooses promising immediate matches but sometimes makes random moves.
Hard CPUMoves about every 0.28 seconds. Looks one move ahead and considers follow-up matches and chains.

Computer difficulty controls how quickly and strategically the computer plays. It does not change the rules for your own blocks.
